Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.

Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. Backlog-driven proportional correction: node0 reduces order when backlog exceeds pipeline plus arrival; node1 increases order when backlog is high and pipeline is low; node2 increases order when inventory is low and backlog is zero to prevent future stockout.

Growth-aware and pipeline-aware: node0 reduces order when recent demand growth is low and backlog is high; node1 increases order when growth is low and backlog is high to rebuild pipeline; node2 increases order when inventory is low and pipeline is low.

candidates.explanation: Coordinated pipeline-aware relaxation: node0 reduces order when backlog is high and pipeline is sufficient, while upstream nodes maintain or slightly increase orders to replenish depleted inventories. This avoids further starving downstream while preventing excessive upstream backlog.

Demand-responsive correction: when recent demand exceeds baseline (growth>1), increase orders at all nodes to rebuild inventory and reduce backlog; when growth<1, decrease orders to avoid overstock. Uses growth ratio to scale correction.
Backlog-clearing priority: if any node has backlog and inventory is zero, increase order to replenish, but cap increase to avoid overshoot. Upstream nodes get larger increases to ensure supply.
